A HAZOP, as an accepted process hazard analysis (PHA) methodology, must address both facility siting and human factors, rather than focusing only on equipment failures [1][3]. 

Under 29 CFR 1910.119(e)(3), the process hazard analysis must address all of the following:
- The hazards of the process [1][2][3].
- The identification of any previous incident which had a likely potential for catastrophic consequences in the workplace [1][2][3].
- Engineering and administrative controls applicable to the hazards and their interrelationships, such as appropriate detection methodologies [1][2][3].
- Consequences of failure of engineering and administrative controls [1][2][3].
- Facility siting [1][2][3].
- Human factors [1][2][3].
- A qualitative evaluation of a range of the possible safety and health effects of failure of controls on employees in the workplace [1][2][3].

Additionally, a PHA focuses on equipment, instrumentation, utilities, human actions (routine and nonroutine), and external factors that might impact the process [5].

An inert gas (such as nitrogen) blanketing system is required on a cone-roof tank storing a flammable material with an electrical conductivity of 10 pS/m or less in the following cases [4][5]:

* When the capacity of the cone-roof tank is 100 m3 or more [4].
* When the capacity of the cone-roof tank is less than 100 m3 and static electricity can form under either of the following conditions [4]:
  * The storage tank is filled while the flammable material is sprayed from the internal inlet nozzle [4].
  * The inlet flow velocity of the flammable material is 1.0 m/s or higher [4].

However, an inert gas blanketing system must not be installed if the stored material is unstable and contains a chemical reaction inhibitor that requires oxygen [4].

An incident investigation must be initiated as promptly as possible, but not later than 48 hours following the incident [1][2][3]. 

This requirement applies to each incident—including "near misses" where serious consequences did not occur but could have—that resulted in, or could reasonably have resulted in, a catastrophic release of a highly hazardous chemical in the workplace [1][2][3][4].

Yes, the study must address facility siting and human factors, and cannot focus solely on equipment failures [1][2][3][4]. 

When conducting a process hazard analysis (PHA) using HAZOP or any other approved methodology, the analysis must address [1][2][3][5]:
- Facility siting [1][2][3]
- Human factors [1][2][3]
- The hazards of the process [1][2][3]
- The identification of any previous incident that had a likely potential for catastrophic consequences in the workplace [1][2][3]
- Applicable engineering and administrative controls and their interrelationships [1][2][3]
- Consequences of failure of engineering and administrative controls [1][2][3]
- A qualitative evaluation of possible safety and health effects on employees if controls fail [1][2][3]

Additionally, the PHA is directed to focus not only on equipment, but also on instrumentation, utilities, routine and nonroutine human actions, and external factors impacting the process [4].

No, the process safety contractor requirements do not apply to them [1][2][3]. 

The contractor requirements apply to contractors performing maintenance or repair, turnaround, major renovation, or specialty work on or adjacent to a covered process [1][2][3]. They do not apply to contractors providing incidental services that do not influence process safety, such as janitorial work, food and drink services, laundry, delivery, or other supply services [1][2][3].

A process is brought into scope if it involves a flammable liquid or gas on site in one location in a quantity of 10,000 pounds (4535.9 kg) or more [1][2][3]. 

Under 29 CFR 1910.119(a)(1)(ii), this covers a flammable liquid or gas (specified in later editions as a Category 1 flammable gas or a flammable liquid with a flashpoint below 100 °F (37.8 °C)), subject to the following exceptions [1][2]:
- Hydrocarbon fuels used solely for workplace consumption as a fuel (e.g., propane used for comfort heating, gasoline for vehicle refueling), provided they are not part of a process containing another highly hazardous chemical covered by the standard [1][2].
- Flammable liquids (or flammable liquids with a flashpoint below 100 °F (37.8 °C)) stored in atmospheric tanks or transferred that are kept below their normal boiling point without benefit of chilling or refrigeration [1][2].

No, you do not have to include material and energy balances in its process safety information [1][2][3][4]. Under PSM, material and energy balances are only required for processes built after May 26, 1992 [1][2][3][4].
사업주는 운전절차서가 오래되거나 부정확해지는 것을 방지하기 위해 매년(annually) 해당 운전절차서가 최신 상태이고 정확하다는 것을 확인하여 인증해야 합니다 [1].

미국 PSM(OSHA) 기준에서 공정이나 설비 등을 변경하기 전 변경관리(MOC) 절차를 통해 반드시 검토하고 다루어야 하는 항목은 다음과 같습니다 [2].

* 제안된 변경에 대한 기술적 근거 (The technical basis for the proposed change) [2]
* 변경이 근로자의 안전 및 보건에 미치는 영향 (Impact of the change on employee safety and health) [2]
* 운전절차서의 수정 사항 (Modifications to operating procedures) [2]
* 변경에 필요한 기간 (Necessary time period for the change) [2]
* 제안된 변경에 대한 승인 요건 (Authorization requirements for the proposed change) [2]

OSHA PSM의 기계적 건전성(Mechanical Integrity) 요건은 다음의 공정 설비들에 적용됩니다 [1][5]:

- 압력용기 및 저장탱크(Pressure vessels and storage tanks) [1][5]
- 밸브 등의 배관 구성요소를 포함하는 배관 시스템(Piping systems (including piping components such as valves)) [1][5]
- 방출 및 벤트 시스템과 장치(Relief and vent systems and devices) [1][5]
- 비상 차단 시스템(Emergency shutdown systems) [1][5]
- 모니터링 장치 및 센서, 경보, 인터록을 포함하는 제어 장치(Controls (including monitoring devices and sensors, alarms, and interlocks)) [1][5]
- 펌프(Pumps) [1][5]

영업비밀(Trade secret) 정보라는 이유로 공정위험성평가 개발 담당자나 사고조사 참여자에게 필요한 공정 정보를 제한해서는 안 됩니다 [1][2]. 

고용주는 해당 정보의 영업비밀 해당 여부와 상관없이(without regard to possible trade secret status), PSM을 준수하는 데 필요한 모든 정보를 공정안전자료 수집 담당자, 공정위험성평가(process hazard analysis) 개발 담당자, 운전절차 개발 담당자, 사고조사(incident investigations) 참여자, 비상대응계획 및 대응 담당자, 이행 감사 담당자에게 제공해야 합니다 [1][2]. 

다만, 고용주가 정보를 제공받는 대상자들에게 해당 정보를 공개하지 않도록 하는 비밀유지 계약(confidentiality agreements)을 체결하도록 요구하는 것은 금지되지 않습니다 [1][2].

임시 공정 배관 연결과 같은 임시변경도 변경관리에 포함하여 해당 절차에 따라 실시하여야 합니다 [1][2][4]. 

임시변경의 기간은 단시간 내에 실시되어야(단기간 내 일시적으로 이루어져야) 하며, 변경이 완료되면 해당 설비는 원상복구하여야 합니다 [1][5].
설정압력이 게이지 압력으로 5 bar 미만인 경우에 해당하므로, 허용 오차범위는 ±0.14 bar 이하입니다 [1].
질소 블랭킷(불활성가스 봉입시설)이 설치된 고정식 지붕탱크(콘루프 탱크)의 설계압력은 양압 2,000 Pa(0.0204 ㎏/㎠) 이내, 진공압력 600 Pa(0.0061 ㎏/㎠) 이내로 하여야 합니다 [1][3].

A floating-roof tank must not be used in the following cases [4]:

* When the stored material is contaminated or affected by the infiltration of rainwater [4].
* When there is a risk of toxic substance vapors leaking [4].
* When the stored material has a high viscosity or a high freezing point, thereby forming a thick film on the inner surface of the tank at room temperature (unless the floating-roof tank is insulated or heated to prevent the formation of such a film) [4]. 

(Floating-roof tanks are generally used for storing large quantities of flammable materials with a flash point of 23 ℃ or lower to minimize vapor loss to the atmosphere, subject to the restrictions above) [4].
상압저장탱크의 설계온도는 저장물질의 온도에 30 ℃를 더한 수치로 정합니다 [1]. 다만, 스팀을 사용하여 상압저장탱크를 청소할 필요가 있는 경우에는 설계온도를 120 ℃로 적용하여 다르게 정합니다 [1].

An inert gas blanketing (inerting) system is required on a cone-roof tank storing a flammable liquid with an electrical conductivity of 10 pS/m or less under the following conditions [4][5]:

1. The capacity of the cone-roof tank is 100 m3 or more [4].
2. The capacity of the cone-roof tank is less than 100 m3 and static electricity can be generated because:
   - The flammable liquid is filled while spraying from an internal inlet nozzle, or [4]
   - The inlet flow velocity of the flammable liquid is 1.0 m/s or higher [4].

따라서 해당 조건(섭씨 350도 이상 또는 게이지 압력 980킬로파스칼 이상)에서 운전되거나, 발열반응이 일어나는 반응장치 또는 증류ㆍ정류ㆍ증발ㆍ추출 등 분리를 하는 장치에 해당하는 특수화학설비를 설치할 때 내부 이상 상태를 조기에 파악하기 위한 온도계ㆍ유량계ㆍ압력계 등의 계측장치를 설치하여야 합니다 [1].
화학설비 및 그 부속설비를 계속하여 1개월 이상 사용하지 아니한 후 다시 사용하는 경우에 안전검사내용을 점검한 후 가동(사용)해야 합니다 [1]. 아울러 해당 설비를 분해하거나 개조 또는 수리를 한 경우에도 사용 전 점검을 실시해야 합니다 [1].

동일하게 전면 금지되는 것은 아니며, 예외적으로 차단밸브를 설치할 수 있습니다 [2].

원칙적으로 안전보건규칙 제266조에 따라 안전밸브등의 전단 및 후단에는 차단밸브를 설치할 수 없습니다 [2]. 다만, 열팽창에 의하여 상승된 압력을 낮추기 위한 목적으로 안전밸브가 설치된 경우에는 자물쇠형 또는 이에 준하는 형식의 차단밸브를 설치할 수 있습니다 [2].

The second relief valve does not have to be set at or below the maximum allowable working pressure; it can be set higher [1][2]. 

When two or more safety valves are installed, one valve can be installed to operate at up to 1.05 times (105% of) the maximum allowable working pressure for non-fire cases, and up to 1.1 times (110% of) the maximum allowable working pressure if prepared for external fire [1][2].

A pressure relief device (safety valve or rupture disk) is mandatory only in certain configurations, not on every positive displacement pump [2][4]. Under Article 261(1) Item 3 of the Occupational Safety and Health Standards Rules, it is required only for positive displacement pumps that have a shut-off valve installed on the discharge side [2][4]. 

However, installation is not required if an equivalent protective device is provided instead [2][4].

No, you do not have to install gas detection and alarm devices [1]. 

Under Article 232(2) of the Rules on Occupational Safety and Health Standards, employers are generally required to install gas detection and alarm systems to detect explosions or fires in advance; however, an exception applies if the location corresponds to a Zone 0 or Zone 1 explosion-hazardous area under Korean Industrial Standards and explosion-proof electrical machinery and apparatus have been installed in accordance with Article 311 [1].
